note: HER2-positive gastric xenografts called pertuzumab plus trastuzumab a winner and JACOB missed overall survival; margetuximab's Fc-optimisation prediction was never isolated in single-arm gastric trials; the trastuzumab/pertuzumab-derived biparatopic anbenitamab matched its xenografts in the phase 3 KC-WISE.
label: Gastric cancer (anti-HER2 mAb)

engagement.model: HER2-positive human gastric cancer xenografts (NCI-N87, 4-1ST) in mice, pertuzumab plus trastuzumab
engagement.note: Model read EGFR-HER2 and HER2-HER3 heterodimer and phospho-signalling inhibition in xenografts; no tumour PD readout was taken in gastric patients in JOSHUA or JACOB.
engagement.short: Heterodimer PD never read in patients
engagement.quote: Combining pertuzumab with trastuzumab enhanced cell growth inhibition and apoptosis activity by inhibiting EGFR-HER2 heterodimerization and the phosphorylation of these receptors and their downstream factors.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Clin Cancer Res, paywalled). The JOSHUA and JACOB abstracts report no on-treatment tumour pharmacodynamic measurement.
engagement.reason: No PD comparison in gastric patients
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at the first pertuzumab use in a gastric model. The model's readouts (heterodimer PLA, phospho-HER2/HER3/AKT, ADCC, microvessel density) were never measured in margetuximab- or pertuzumab-treated gastric patients, so nothing can be compared. Trastuzumab, which used the same xenograft line earlier, is not a member of this class.

engagement.model: Fc-optimised anti-HER2 ADCC assays with CD16A-genotyped donor effectors (N87 and SKBR-3 targets) and human CD16A-158F transgenic mice bearing JIMT-1 xenografts
engagement.note: Model readout was ADCC by CD16A-158F effectors and NK activation; no NK or ADCC pharmacodynamic readout was reported in margetuximab-treated gastric patients.
engagement.short: ADCC readout not measured in patients
engagement.quote: The greatest improvement occurs with effector cells isolated from donors homozygous or heterozygous for CD16A-158F, the low-binding allele.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Nordstrom 2011 (open access, not read in full) and of Catenacci 2020 and 2022, whose abstracts list pharmacodynamics as a secondary objective without reporting an NK, ADCC or CD16A-genotype result; a genotype analysis in the full text, if any, was not checked. model_kind animal because the hCD16A-158F mouse is the system's distinctive part; the N87 ADCC assay is ex vivo.
engagement.reason: No ADCC PD read in gastric patients
engagement.judgement: Opening entry. The FDA review of BLA 761150 (sources/761150) confirms the N87 gastric line was an ADCC target in the filed pharmacology, so model_filed is true. The regulator's own CD16A-158V/V efficacy anomaly concerns breast cancer and is not an engagement readout.

engagement.model: Trastuzumab/pertuzumab-derived anti-HER2 bispecific on Alphamab's heterodimeric (CRIB) Fc, cancer-cell proliferation in vitro and in mouse xenografts
engagement.note: Model readout was cancer-cell proliferation in vitro and in vivo; no HER2-pathway pharmacodynamic readout was reported in anbenitamab-treated gastric patients.
engagement.quote: An anti-HER2 bispecific antibody derived from trastuzumab and pertuzumab was generated by this heterodimeric Fc.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The abstract names neither KN026 nor the cell lines, so product_in_model is unknown; KN026/anbenitamab is Alphamab's trastuzumab-plus-pertuzumab-epitope biparatopic on this Fc platform (Zhang 2022, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-21-2827). No dedicated KN026 preclinical paper was found in PubMed/Europe PMC.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry for a separate track: a biparatopic single molecule tested after trastuzumab failure is a different system and a different prediction from the pertuzumab-plus-trastuzumab xenografts, so it does not share the N87 track.
engagement.population: HER2-positive cancer cell lines and xenografts

dose.model: HER2-positive human gastric cancer xenografts (NCI-N87, 4-1ST) in mice, pertuzumab plus trastuzumab
dose.note: Xenograft doses set no human target; the 20 µg/mL trough target came from breast xenografts and gastric patients ran ~37% lower troughs (JOSHUA).
dose.short: Gastric model set no exposure target
dose.quote: Pertuzumab in combination with trastuzumab showed significant antitumor activity compared with each monotherapy in NCI-N87, an HER2-positive human gastric cancer xenograft model.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. The programme's only exposure target, a serum trough of 20 µg/mL, is documented in the Perjeta EPAR (non-clinical dose-response studies) and the Phesgo review (sources/761170: 'nonclinical mouse xenograft models and early clinical response data'); neither names a gastric model.
dose.judgement: Opening entry; no gastric-model exposure target existed, so nothing was reached or missed until JOSHUA and JACOB tested the breast-derived target.

dose.model: HER2-positive human gastric cancer xenografts (NCI-N87, 4-1ST) in mice, pertuzumab plus trastuzumab
dose.note: JOSHUA reached the 20 µg/mL target (day-43 Cmin 62.7 µg/mL at 840 mg q3w); JACOB used that dose and missed OS.
dose.quote: overall survival was not significantly different between treatment groups (median overall survival 17·5 months [95% CI 16·2-19·3] in the pertuzumab group and 14·2 months [12·9-15·5] in the control group; hazard ratio 0·84 [95% CI 0·71-1·00]; p=0·057)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of JACOB and of JOSHUA (Kang 2014, doi 10.1038/bjc.2014.356; NCT01461057 results posted 2016-06-27, co-primary endpoint day-43 pertuzumab Cmin >= 20 µg/mL: mean 40.0 µg/mL at 840/420 mg, 62.7 µg/mL at 840 mg q3w). The 20 µg/mL target was derived in breast, not gastric, models (Perjeta EPAR; Phesgo review).
dose.judgement: Table row 'reached, failed, abandoned': the programme's only exposure target (serum trough >= 20 µg/mL) was met in gastric patients at the 840 mg q3w dose chosen after JOSHUA, and JACOB then missed its primary endpoint, so the failure is counted once in efficacy and derived here. Not left untested as in a no-target cell-line case because an explicit target existed and JOSHUA was run to test it. The monkey tolerability finding (no NOAEL, decision 16) is scored in safety, not here, because patients were dosed to target.
dose.population: First-line HER2-positive metastatic gastric/GEJ cancer, pertuzumab 840 mg q3w with trastuzumab and cisplatin-fluoropyrimidine

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey single and repeat-dose toxicology and toxicokinetics of MGAH22 (margetuximab)
dose.note: Monkeys tolerated 15-150 mg/kg with antibody-typical PK; no human exposure target was stated, and the clinical dose awaited the phase 1.
dose.short: Monkey margin stated, no human target
dose.quote: MGAH22 was well tolerated at all doses tested (15-150 mg/kg) and exhibited pharmacokinetic parameters similar to that of other anti-HER2 antibodies.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the quote is a verbatim fragment of a longer sentence. The ADCC/hCD16A-158F track stated no exposure target and so has no dose entry; the tolerability margin is the monkey's, hence this track.
dose.judgement: Opening entry on the monkey track because decision 16 scores the toxic end of the window and the margin was stated by the monkey, not by the ADCC model.

dose.model: Cynomolgus monkey single and repeat-dose toxicology and toxicokinetics of MGAH22 (margetuximab)
dose.note: Gastric patients took the 15 mg/kg q3w phase 2 dose with pembrolizumab without dose-limiting toxicity, inside the monkey's 15-150 mg/kg tolerated range.
dose.quote: The combination therapy showed acceptable safety and tolerability; there were no dose-limiting toxicities in the dose-escalation phase.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Decision 16: the model stated a tolerated dose at or above the clinical dose and it held. Whether 15 mg/kg q3w was enough is untested because every gastric margetuximab trial was single-arm (see efficacy). Registry results for NCT02689284 posted 2022-08-04, after the 2020 paper.
dose.reason: Monkey tolerability margin held in patients
dose.judgement: Same with margin_stated under decision 16, direction only: the 15 mg/kg q3w dose (selected in breast for activity similar to 6 mg/kg weekly, FDA review sources/761150) sits at the bottom of the monkey's tolerated range and produced no DLT in gastric patients. Paired by me; the trial paper does not cite the monkey data.
dose.magnitude_basis: tolerated dose: monkeys 15-150 mg/kg weekly versus patients 15 mg/kg every 3 weeks without dose-limiting toxicity
dose.population: HER2-positive gastro-oesophageal adenocarcinoma after trastuzumab, margetuximab 15 mg/kg q3w plus pembrolizumab

dose.model: Trastuzumab/pertuzumab-derived anti-HER2 bispecific on Alphamab's heterodimeric (CRIB) Fc, cancer-cell proliferation in vitro and in mouse xenografts
dose.note: Bispecific xenografts set no human exposure target; the 30 mg/kg q3w gastric dose came from exposure-response in the breast phase 1.
dose.quote: It showed comparable or improved efficacy than the combination of trastuzumab and pertuzumab in inhibiting proliferation of cancer cells in vitro and in vivo.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; xenograft doses are not in the abstract. The recommended phase 2 doses (20 mg/kg q2w or 30 mg/kg q3w) came from clinical exposure-response in HER2-positive breast cancer (Zhang 2022, doi 10.1158/1078-0432.CCR-21-2827); KC-WISE used 30 mg/kg q3w.
dose.judgement: Untested rather than same despite the positive phase 3: the model stated no exposure, occupancy or regimen target, so nothing it said about dose was reached or missed; the efficacy success is counted once, in efficacy.
dose.population: HER2-positive cancer cell lines and xenografts

dose.note: Xenograft dose-response fixed a 20 µg/mL trough as the effective exposure; the breast regimen was chosen to reach it. No gastric patient exposure or outcome yet.
dose.quote: The serum pertuzumab concentration of 20 μg/mL was set as a target serum concentration based on the observation that the maximum suppression of tumor growth was achieved at ~5 - 25 μg/mL in xenograft mouse models.
dose.confidence_note: Regulator text read in full (curl + pdftotext; the review is not in the source bundle). The underlying xenograft study is Malik 2003, Proc Am Assoc Cancer Res 44:150 (AACR abstract, no DOI), named by the Phesgo review (sources/761170) as the origin of the target together with early clinical response data; the 2012 FDA and EMA reviews are the earliest public statements of the target, so the track opens there. The gastric application began with JOSHUA (NCT01461057, posted 2011-10-27), whose co-primary endpoint was the day-43 pertuzumab trough.
dose.judgement: Separate track from the NCI-N87/4-1ST gastric xenografts (decision 8, checker rule question 2): the exposure target was stated by non-gastric xenografts, not by the gastric efficacy model, so the dose table's 'reached, failed' row belongs to the system that stated the target. Opening untested: a target existed, no gastric patient had been dosed to it when it was stated. model_filed true because the target sits in the pertuzumab BLA clinical pharmacology review.
dose.population: HER2-overexpressing xenograft lines (breast, NSCLC and other non-gastric); regimen selection for HER2-positive breast cancer
dose.model: Pertuzumab serum exposure target (trough >= 20 µg/mL) set from maximal tumour-growth suppression at ~5-25 µg/mL in HER2-overexpressing mouse xenografts (non-gastric lines, Malik 2003), carried into gastric dosing by JOSHUA and JACOB

dose.note: Target reached in gastric patients: JOSHUA day-43 trough 62.7 µg/mL at 840 mg q3w, JACOB's PK paper says the majority reached target; JACOB then missed OS, so the exposure was not enough.
dose.quote: overall survival was not significantly different between treatment groups (median overall survival 17·5 months [95% CI 16·2-19·3] in the pertuzumab group and 14·2 months [12·9-15·5] in the control group; hazard ratio 0·84 [95% CI 0·71-1·00]; p=0·057)
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Kang 2014 (JOSHUA, doi 10.1038/bjc.2014.356: mean day-43 Cmin 40.0 µg/mL at 840/420 mg, 62.7 µg/mL at 840 mg q3w, the latter chosen for phase 3) and of Kirschbrown 2019 (doi 10.1007/s00280-019-03871-w: 'The 840 mg q3w dose allowed the majority of patients in JACOB to achieve target pertuzumab concentrations'). JACOB OS was first public at ESMO 2017 (abstract 616O); year 2018 follows the draft's JACOB entries pending the checker's dating question.
dose.reason: Exposure target reached, no OS benefit
dose.judgement: Dose table row 'reached, failed, abandoned': the only exposure target the programme stated (trough >= 20 µg/mL, from xenografts) was met in gastric patients at the 840 mg q3w dose JOSHUA selected, and JACOB missed its primary endpoint; the failure is counted once in efficacy on the gastric-xenograft track and derived here. Paired by me: Tabernero 2018 does not set the xenograft target beside the result; Kirschbrown 2019 states the target was reached but does not score the model. Not blocked by toxicity and no tolerability margin came from this model (margin_stated false), so decision 16 does not apply. Trastuzumab's exposure is not scored (not a member).
dose.population: First-line HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+/ISH+) metastatic gastric/GEJ cancer, JACOB n=780 (374 with evaluable pertuzumab PK); JOSHUA phase 2a n=30
dose.model: Pertuzumab serum exposure target (trough >= 20 µg/mL) set from maximal tumour-growth suppression at ~5-25 µg/mL in HER2-overexpressing mouse xenografts (non-gastric lines, Malik 2003), carried into gastric dosing by JOSHUA and JACOB

efficacy.model: HER2-positive human gastric cancer xenografts (NCI-N87, 4-1ST) in mice, pertuzumab plus trastuzumab
efficacy.note: Pertuzumab plus trastuzumab beat each antibody's maximum effective dose in NCI-N87 and 4-1ST HER2-positive gastric xenografts; authors proposed clinical benefit.
efficacy.short: Dual blockade beat monotherapy in gastric xenografts
efficacy.quote: This study suggests the clinical benefit of combination therapy with pertuzumab and trastuzumab for patients with HER2-positive gastric cancers.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Clin Cancer Res, paywalled). The HER2-negative MKN-28 xenograft did not respond, so the model also predicted HER2 selection.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the first pertuzumab use in a gastric model (Chugai, the Roche partner that ran JOSHUA and JACOB). Class-level prediction: adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab helps HER2-positive gastric cancer.

efficacy.model: HER2-positive human gastric cancer xenografts (NCI-N87, 4-1ST) in mice, pertuzumab plus trastuzumab
efficacy.note: JACOB primary OS missed: HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.71-1.00), p=0.057, 17.5 vs 14.2 months; end-of-study analysis (2022) confirmed.
efficacy.quote: Adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab and chemotherapy did not significantly improve overall survival in patients with HER2-positive metastatic gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer compared with placebo.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Lancet Oncol, paywalled); the abstract carries the primary result. Registry results for NCT01774786 posted 2018-02-14, before the 2018-09-11 epub. The end-of-study analysis (Tabernero 2022, doi 10.1007/s10120-022-01335-4) confirmed no significant OS gain.
efficacy.judgement: Primary endpoint governs: OS HR 0.84 with p=0.057 misses. The direction favoured pertuzumab, so the model over-called the size rather than the sign, but v3 scores the primary endpoint, not the trend. JOSHUA (phase 2a, NCT01461057) had PK and safety primaries, so its 86% and 55% partial-response rates change nothing. Paired by me: JACOB does not set the xenograft beside its result. The ToGA trastuzumab success on the same xenograft system is not scored because trastuzumab is not a member of this class.
efficacy.population: First-line HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+/ISH+) metastatic gastric/GEJ cancer, 30 countries, n=780

patient_trials.quote: overall survival was not significantly different between treatment groups (median overall survival 17·5 months [95% CI 16·2-19·3] in the pertuzumab group and 14·2 months [12·9-15·5] in the control group; hazard ratio 0·84 [95% CI 0·71-1·00]; p=0·057)

efficacy.model: Fc-optimised anti-HER2 ADCC assays with CD16A-genotyped donor effectors (N87 and SKBR-3 targets) and human CD16A-158F transgenic mice bearing JIMT-1 xenografts
efficacy.note: Fc-optimised antibody out-performed wild-type Fc in CD16A-158F transgenic mice; predicted benefit for low-binding-allele carriers and low-HER2 tumours.
efficacy.short: Fc-optimised mAb beat wild-type in 158F mice
efficacy.quote: MGAH22 demonstrates increased activity against HER2-expressing tumors in mice transgenic for human CD16A-158F.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (open access, not read in full). The FDA review (sources/761150) adds that the modified Fc binds mouse Fc receptors differently, so 'results from mouse xenograft models with human tumor cells may be limited in evaluating the anti-tumor effects of the modified Fc domain'.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. Patient-level prediction: CD16A-158F carriers, who gain least from trastuzumab, gain from the optimised Fc; the class-level claim (activity in HER2-expressing tumours) rides with it.

efficacy.model: Fc-optimised anti-HER2 ADCC assays with CD16A-genotyped donor effectors (N87 and SKBR-3 targets) and human CD16A-158F transgenic mice bearing JIMT-1 xenografts
efficacy.note: Gastric trials were single-arm with anti-PD-1 (ORR 18% post-trastuzumab, 53% first-line); the randomised MAHOGANY arm versus trastuzumab was discontinued unread.
efficacy.short: Fc effect never isolated in gastric
efficacy.quote: The study sponsor discontinued the study in advance of the planned enrollment when it became apparent that the study design would no longer meet the requirements for drug approval because of recent advances in the treatment of GEA.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of both trial papers. In breast cancer the FDA review of BLA 761150 (SOPHIA) found the CD16A-158V/V subgroup 'in a direction unfavorable to margetuximab' and called it 'mechanistically unexpected'; that is another disease and is not scored here. MAHOGANY cohort B (margetuximab plus chemotherapy with or without retifanlimab versus trastuzumab plus chemotherapy) never reported efficacy; NCT04082364 results posted 2025-04-22 cover cohort A.
efficacy.reason: Single-arm combos never tested Fc prediction
efficacy.judgement: Untested, not same: both gastric trials combined margetuximab with a PD-1 antibody and had no anti-HER2 comparator, so the model's prediction (optimised Fc beats wild-type Fc, most in CD16A-158F carriers) was never compared, and the authors themselves frame CP-MGAH22-05 as proof of concept for synergy with pembrolizumab. The only randomised comparison was discontinued for strategic reasons before any readout. The responses are recorded in patient_trials and change no status; a second untested entry is kept because the abandonment of the randomised arm is the event that fixed the cell.
efficacy.population: HER2-positive gastro-oesophageal adenocarcinoma: post-trastuzumab with pembrolizumab (2020, n=95); first-line HER2 IHC 3+/PD-L1+ with retifanlimab (2022, n=43)

patient_trials.quote: Objective responses were observed in 17 (18·48%; 95% CI 11·15-27·93) of 92 evaluable patients.

The ORR by independent assessment was 53% [21/40 (95% confidence interval (CI) 36.1-68.5)], with a median duration of response of 10.3 months (95% CI 4.6-not evaluable); disease control rate was 73% [29/40 (95% CI 56.1-85.4)].

efficacy.model: Trastuzumab/pertuzumab-derived anti-HER2 bispecific on Alphamab's heterodimeric (CRIB) Fc, cancer-cell proliferation in vitro and in mouse xenografts
efficacy.note: Trastuzumab/pertuzumab-derived biparatopic matched or beat the two-antibody combination in vitro and in xenografts; no patient data yet.
efficacy.quote: It showed comparable or improved efficacy than the combination of trastuzumab and pertuzumab in inhibiting proliferation of cancer cells in vitro and in vivo.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the abstract names neither KN026 nor the tumour lines, so product_in_model is unknown and the gastric relevance of the xenograft is unverified.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry. Class-level prediction: one biparatopic molecule reproduces the trastuzumab-plus-pertuzumab effect in HER2-positive tumours.
efficacy.population: HER2-positive cancer cell lines and xenografts

efficacy.model: Trastuzumab/pertuzumab-derived anti-HER2 bispecific on Alphamab's heterodimeric (CRIB) Fc, cancer-cell proliferation in vitro and in mouse xenografts
efficacy.note: Single-arm phase 2: KN026 monotherapy ORR 56% in HER2-high gastric/GEJ cancer after prior therapy; primary endpoint ORR.
efficacy.quote: The ORR in the high-level HER2 cohort was 56% (95% confidence interval [CI] 35%-76%)
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Eur J Cancer, paywalled; epub 2022-10-19, print 2023); the pre-specified ORR bar is not in the abstract, and the quote is a verbatim fragment. NCT03925974 has no posted results, so registry_date is null. Single-arm, so direction only.
efficacy.judgement: Scored same, unlike the margetuximab single-arm trials, because this was monotherapy: the response is attributable to the bispecific and tests the model's activity prediction in direction. The model's own comparator (trastuzumab plus pertuzumab) was not in the trial, so magnitude is direction only and confidence low.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: monotherapy objective response in HER2-high tumours against xenograft growth inhibition relative to trastuzumab plus pertuzumab
efficacy.population: Previously treated advanced HER2-expressing gastric/GEJ cancer, China; HER2-high cohort n=27

patient_trials.quote: The ORR in the high-level HER2 cohort was 56% (95% confidence interval [CI] 35%-76%)

efficacy.model: Trastuzumab/pertuzumab-derived anti-HER2 bispecific on Alphamab's heterodimeric (CRIB) Fc, cancer-cell proliferation in vitro and in mouse xenografts
efficacy.note: Phase 3 KC-WISE interim: anbenitamab plus chemotherapy beat chemotherapy on both co-primaries after trastuzumab failure, PFS HR 0.25 and OS HR 0.29.
efficacy.quote: Compared with chemotherapy alone, anbenitamab plus chemotherapy demonstrated clinically meaningful superior PFS and OS in patients with HER2-positive GC/GEJ adenocarcinoma whose previous therapy containing trastuzumab had failed.
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading (Ann Oncol; epub 2026-01-20, print 2026-06). Prespecified interim analysis at about 120 PFS events; final analysis pending; NCT05427383 results not posted as of 2026-11-05. The China approval of 27 May 2026 (Blair 2026, doi 10.1007/s40265-026-02382-2) is noted, not used to set the status.
efficacy.reason: Bispecific xenograft call held in phase 3
efficacy.judgement: Strengthens the 2022 same: a randomised, double-blind phase 3 met both co-primary endpoints in trastuzumab-pretreated HER2-positive gastric cancer. Direction only: the trial comparator was chemotherapy, not the trastuzumab-plus-pertuzumab combination the model benchmarked against. Paired by me; the trial paper's rationale is clinical, and whether it cites Wei 2017 was not checked.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PFS and OS hazard ratios versus chemotherapy against xenograft growth inhibition relative to trastuzumab plus pertuzumab
efficacy.population: HER2-positive gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma after trastuzumab failure, 51 Chinese sites, n=188, anbenitamab 30 mg/kg q3w plus taxane or irinotecan

patient_trials.quote: At the prespecified interim analysis, anbenitamab plus chemotherapy significantly improved PFS [median 7.1 months, 95% confidence interval (CI) 5.5-10.3 months versus 2.7 months, 95% CI 1.5-3.0 months; hazard ratio (HR), 0.25, 95% CI 0.17-0.39, P < 0.0001]

efficacy.note: Selection rule proposed: HER2 hyper-amplified (>= 8 copies) gastric patients would benefit from dual blockade. No pertuzumab trial selected or stratified gastric patients by copy number.
efficacy.quote: Our results suggest that a selected subpopulation of HER2-"hyper"-amplified GC patients could strongly benefit from this strategy.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read through the Springer page (Firecrawl); the abstract carries the quote. Searched PubMed and the 20 papers citing Ughetto 2021 (Europe PMC) for a pertuzumab trial in gastric patients selected or analysed by HER2 copy number: none found. JACOB's subgroups are IHC/ISH categories, not copy-number thresholds; NCI-MATCH EAY131-J (NCT06136897, trastuzumab plus pertuzumab in HER2-amplified tumours) excludes gastric/GEJ. The copy-number-to-trastuzumab-benefit data the authors cite (Gomez-Martin) concern trastuzumab, not a member.
efficacy.judgement: Opening entry at the model's first use. The model made two predictions: a class-level one (dual blockade works in HER2-driven gastric cancer), compared below, and a patient-level one (hyper-amplification picks the responders), which nobody has tested in pertuzumab-treated gastric patients. One track, two prediction levels, per the checker's rule question 4; the untested patient-level entry opens the track so the class-level retrodiction can stand as its latest status.
efficacy.population: HER2 hyper-amplified (>= 8 copies) gastric PDX models (n=8)
efficacy.model: HER2 'hyper'-amplified (>= 8 copies) gastric cancer patient-derived xenografts run as preclinical randomized trials of trastuzumab alone versus trastuzumab plus pertuzumab (or lapatinib), 8 models, 5 mice each, RECIST-like response

efficacy.note: Run after JACOB failed: trastuzumab plus pertuzumab gave complete durable responses in 5/8 hyper-amplified PDX, which does not reproduce JACOB's missed OS; the authors set the two against each other.
efficacy.quote: Despite the negative results of clinical trials, the dual blockade should be reconsidered for patients with clearly HER2-addicted cancers.
efficacy.confidence_note: Full text read through the Springer page (Firecrawl); the Discussion states the comparison directly: 'Our results are apparently discordant from the negative ones obtained in the JACOB study' (citing Tabernero 2018). Trastuzumab plus lapatinib arms are pooled with pertuzumab in the 5/8 figure; the pertuzumab-only count was not extracted. Only the PDX arm with a member drug is scored.
efficacy.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the PDX trials were designed and published (epub 2021-03-23) after JACOB's final analysis (ESMO 2017, Lancet Oncol 2018), and the authors frame them against the negative trials. A retrodiction that fails to reproduce the human primary-endpoint result is contra, never retro; the authors' explanation (JACOB's IHC/ISH population was not HER2-addicted) is a patient-level hypothesis recorded as untested above, not a reversal of the class-level comparison. source_calls_it unresolved because the paper attributes the discordance to patient selection rather than conceding a miss. Subjects patients: the human side is JACOB. Pertuzumab was dosed in the PDX (product_in_model true).
efficacy.population: HER2 hyper-amplified (>= 8 copies) gastric PDX (n=8 models) versus JACOB: first-line HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+/ISH+) metastatic gastric/GEJ cancer, n=780

patient_trials.quote: overall survival was not significantly different between treatment groups (median overall survival 17·5 months [95% CI 16·2-19·3] in the pertuzumab group and 14·2 months [12·9-15·5] in the control group; hazard ratio 0·84 [95% CI 0·71-1·00]; p=0·057)

efficacy.model: HER2 'hyper'-amplified (>= 8 copies) gastric cancer patient-derived xenografts run as preclinical randomized trials of trastuzumab alone versus trastuzumab plus pertuzumab (or lapatinib), 8 models, 5 mice each, RECIST-like response

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology, up to 26 weekly doses (pertuzumab)
safety.note: Monkeys had severe secretory diarrhoea, one euthanised; the EPAR calls this in line with diarrhoea in pertuzumab-treated breast patients (imported).
safety.quote: As highlighted, the major non-clinical findings were diarrhoea, liquid and non-formed faeces. This is in line with the clinical studies in which the main adverse events reported with pertuzumab were diarrhoea, fatigue and nausea.
safety.confidence_note: Read from the EPAR text (EMA/17250/2013, 13 December 2012; curl plus pdftotext). The FDA pharmacology review URL for BLA 125409 returned no PDF, so the EPAR is the regulator source; the bundled Perjeta label (sources/125409) mentions the monkey studies only for reproductive organs. The EPAR also states no NOAEL could be set because of diarrhoea at all doses.
safety.judgement: On-target class harm (HER1/HER2 and HER2/HER3 heterodimer blockade), so it pools across indications; imported from breast cancer because the regulator's stated comparison was made on CLEOPATRA. Magnitude direction only: severe with euthanasia in monkeys versus manageable grade 3 diarrhoea in patients, an over-prediction of severity that decision 16 does not score as a dose failure because patients reached target. model_first_use_year null: the EPAR does not date the studies.
safety.magnitude_basis: harm present in both; severe diarrhoea with euthanasia in monkeys versus grade 3 diarrhoea 7.9% vs 5.0% in CLEOPATRA
safety.population: Pertuzumab-treated HER2-positive metastatic breast cancer patients (CLEOPATRA), imported

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey repeat-dose toxicology, up to 26 weekly doses (pertuzumab)
safety.note: In gastric patients grade 3-5 diarrhoea was 13% vs 6% with placebo; the monkey-predicted harm held with cisplatin-fluoropyrimidine.
safety.short: Diarrhoea excess seen in gastric patients
safety.quote: The most common grade 3-5 adverse events were neutropenia (116 [30%] patients in the pertuzumab group vs 108 [28%] patients in the control group), anaemia (56 [15%] vs 65 [17%]), and diarrhoea (51 [13%] vs 25 [6%]).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the diarrhoea excess over placebo (13% vs 6% grade 3-5) is the arm difference on a fluoropyrimidine backbone that itself causes diarrhoea.
safety.reason: Monkey diarrhoea held in gastric patients
safety.judgement: Paired by me: JACOB does not cite the monkey data; the model side is the EPAR. Scored same because the harm the species predicted appeared in gastric patients. No unpredicted harm the monkey could have shown emerged: treatment-related deaths were none with pertuzumab versus seven with placebo, and serious diarrhoea was 4% vs 5%.
safety.magnitude_basis: harm present; 7-point excess in grade 3-5 diarrhoea over placebo plus trastuzumab and chemotherapy
safety.population: First-line HER2-positive metastatic gastric/GEJ cancer, pertuzumab plus trastuzumab and cisplatin-fluoropyrimidine, n=780

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey single and repeat-dose toxicology and toxicokinetics of MGAH22 (margetuximab)
safety.note: Monkeys at 15-150 mg/kg showed no target organ and no cytokine release; no gastric patient had yet been dosed.
safety.short: Monkeys clean, patients not yet dosed
safety.quote: MGAH22 was well tolerated at all doses tested (15-150 mg/kg) and exhibited pharmacokinetic parameters similar to that of other anti-HER2 antibodies.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading; the quote is a verbatim fragment. The filed version (FDA review, sources/761150): 'No target organs for margetuximab were identified, nor were there margetuximab-related increased release of IFN-γ, IL-2, IL-5, IL-6, IL-10, or TNF-α in serum.'
safety.judgement: Opening entry on the monkey track; the monkey was chosen because its Fc receptors bind the optimised Fc, so it could in principle show Fc-driven harms.

safety.model: Cynomolgus monkey single and repeat-dose toxicology and toxicokinetics of MGAH22 (margetuximab)
safety.note: No dose-limiting toxicity or treatment-related death; grade 3-4 anaemia 4% and infusion reactions 3% with pembrolizumab, matching the clean monkey profile.
safety.short: Clean monkey profile held in patients
safety.quote: The most common grade 3-4 treatment-related adverse events were anaemia (four [4%]) and infusion-related reactions (three [3%]).
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading of Catenacci 2020; the model side is read from the bundled FDA review text (sources/761150). Infusion-related reactions (3% grade 3-4) are the one patient harm the general toxicology did not show; the pregnant-monkey ePPND study did record hypersensitivity reactions, so the species can show it.
safety.reason: No unpredicted harm in gastric patients
safety.judgement: Same, not contra, on infusion reactions: they are a platform harm of chimeric IgG1 antibodies, occurred at low grade with pembrolizumab co-administered, and the species did show hypersensitivity in the ePPND study, so the general-tox silence is not a clear miss; a reviewer who weighs infusion reactions more heavily could mark this entry other. The breast-cancer comparison in the FDA review (profile similar to trastuzumab) is not imported because the gastric trial supplies its own.
safety.magnitude_basis: absence of target-organ toxicity in monkeys versus a low-grade patient profile with no DLT or treatment-related death
safety.population: HER2-positive gastro-oesophageal adenocarcinoma after trastuzumab, margetuximab 15 mg/kg q3w plus pembrolizumab, n=95
